result.title: The Surprising Effectiveness of Deleting Weights in LLM Post-Training
result.summary: How little of a pretrained large language model (LLM) has to change for it to acquire new capabilities? We find that zeroing fewer than 0.05% of its weights, with no other modification, matches full fine-tuning (FFT) at scale across three LLM post-training regimes: reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards, supervised fine-tuning, and on-policy distillation. Our method, Deletion Tuning, learns a binary mask over the gate projection of transformer blocks. Two practical advantages follow: the trained mask is hundreds to thousands of times smaller than the corresponding FFT checkpoint, and Deletion Tuning forgets far less, which addresses a central challenge in continual learning. Under reinforcement learning, its prior-task accuracy stays near the base level while FFT, LoRA, and random sparse fine-tuning lose up to 5.4 points. To understand why masking alone suffices, we analyze the geometry of the learned weight changes under reinforcement learning using stable rank, spectrum drift, and principal-weight overlap. Compared with LoRA and random sparse fine-tuning, Deletion Tuning is closest to FFT across the three measures.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Deletion Tuning：在 transformer block 的 gate projection 上学习二值掩码，仅置零不到 0.05% 的权重，即在 RLVR、监督微调和 on-policy 蒸馏三种后训练范式下达到与全量微调相当的效果，并用 stable rank、谱漂移和主权重重叠分析权重变化几何。
AI.relevance_reason: 属纯文本后训练工作，与视觉推理无直接关系；但其「极稀疏掩码更新 + 显著减少遗忘」的训练线索，可供核查是否能在 VLM 的 RL 后训练中保住视觉感知与既有能力、并降低适配存储成本，权重变化几何分析也可能为 latent 状态漂移提供参照。
